headline: Child care centers per resident rank highest citywide in Ward 9, coffee shops rank last.
summary:
Roseland, West Pullman, Riverdale, and Pullman make up Ward 9 on Chicago's Far South Side. Its overall standing is 43rd out of the fifty. A score of 32.29 sits behind that number, below the citywide average.

Family life and faith drive its strongest numbers. Ward 9 has the highest count of child care centers per resident in Chicago, its 311 pothole requests close in about two and a half days on average, the second-fastest turnaround citywide, and mapped houses of worship are denser here than almost anywhere else in the fifty. Commuting and nightlife pull the numbers down. Two in five workers here report a commute of 45 minutes or longer, among the longest stretches in Chicago. The ward has almost no bars or coffee shops by the count used in this report, and it posts the worst reading in the city on a wastewater-proximity index built from environmental justice data. Ward 9 reads as a place organized around home, family, and worship, with little built around nightlife or a short commute.
reading_the_rankings: Take the No. 1 rank in child care centers per resident first. That childcare count is drawn from ZIP code areas instead of ward boundaries, and the two maps don't line up anywhere in the city. Low confidence is attached to this figure too. The last-place rank in coffee shops looks just as stark, until you read the caveat underneath it. Two points also separates Ward 9's last-place coffee-shop count from eleven other wards, so the bottom of this particular ranking sits closer together than the single rank position suggests. The worst mark in the city on wastewater proximity carries the same tract problem as several other measures here. Its source treats every acre of a census tract as if the same number of people lived on it, an assumption that breaks down wherever a tract crosses into the next ward. Strip off the top quarter of wards and the bottom quarter here, and just 3.2 points cover the whole range left in the middle, so one rank spot barely reflects a real difference underneath it.

news.headline: 14 Wounded In 'Horrific' Drive-By Mass Shooting In Roseland, Police Say
news.note: A drive-by shooting into a Juneteenth gathering in the Princeton Park part of Roseland injured 14 people, Chicago's largest mass shooting so far in 2026.
